public_rationale: The quoted construction condition is supported: contemporaneous Dow Jones reporting explicitly limits coverage to completed facilities. NVIDIA's later filing also describes activation by completed phases. This does not mean the guarantee is unrelated to rent: default-related exposure includes defined lease and power obligations. Support applies to the completion condition and residual-value structure, not an absolute exclusion of every lease-related liability.
limitations: The decisive quotation is independent news reporting; the accessible primary filing supplies important qualifications.
A completed phase can activate coverage before the whole campus is built.
A broader interpretation excluding all lease-payment exposure would not receive this supported outcome.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns the Ohio agreement described immediately before the post, announced on August 17, 2026.
The plain reading is that the backstop becomes operative for completed, service-ready facilities or phases, rather than construction expenditure.
Completion of every planned phase is not required before any guarantee can apply.

The surrounding contrast with ongoing lease payments is read as residual-value protection rather than routine payment of OpenAI's rent. It does not mean lease defaults can never trigger NVIDIA's liability.
criteria.support_condition: The reported agreement makes the backstop operative upon completion or readiness for service of the applicable facilities and protects residual value rather than financing unfinished construction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The agreement makes NVIDIA liable for unfinished construction regardless of delivery or requires it to pay ordinary ongoing rent independently of the completed-asset backstop.
